lessons.title: Nazra Quran Majeed — Paras 7 to 12
lessons.notes_html:
The Holy Quran — Introduction

Islam is a universal and everlasting religion. Its foundation is the Holy Quran and the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet ﷺ.

  • The Holy Quran is the last Book of Allah Almighty.
  • Allah Almighty revealed it to the last Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ, through Hazrat Jibrail Ameen (AS).
  • The Holy Quran is guidance and a complete code of life for the welfare of all mankind.
  • The solution of the problems of every walk of life is present in the Holy Quran.
  • The Holy Quran is the source of guidance and the foundation of the religion of Islam.

What is Nazra?

Nazra means reading the Holy Quran by looking at it. For this class, six paras are fixed for Nazra reading: Para 7 to Para 12.

  • Para 7: Wa Idha Sami'u
  • Para 8: Wa Lau Annana
  • Para 9: Qalal Mala'u
  • Para 10: Wa A'lamu
  • Para 11: Ya'tazirun
  • Para 12: Wa Ma Min Da'bbah

These paras must be read with correct pronunciation and vowels (I'rab), with Qira'at and Tajweed, in a pleasant voice and with fluency. After learning the translation of the Holy Quran, students will be able to join its teachings with their practical life.

Important Points about the Exam

  • An exam of this part will be taken during the year, and at the annual exam there will be an oral (viva) exam of it.
  • A total of forty percent (40%) marks are fixed for this part.
  • The marks obtained in this part will be entered separately in the result sheet.
  • Passing this part is compulsory for passing the subject of Islamiat.
  • The teacher should teach the students to read the Holy Quran with correct pronunciation.

Rights of the Holy Quran

The Holy Quran has four great rights upon us:

  • To recite the Holy Quran with Qira'at and Tajweed.
  • To think and ponder over the Holy Quran.
  • To act upon the teachings of the Holy Quran.
  • To convey the teachings of the Holy Quran to others, that is, to preach them.

mcqs.q: Through whom did Allah Almighty reveal the Holy Quran to Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Jibrail Ameen (AS). The book's introduction tells us that Allah Almighty sent down the Holy Quran to the Holy Prophet ﷺ through Jibrail Ameen. That is why he is called the angel of revelation.

mcqs.q: In the introduction of the book, the Holy Quran has been called the foundation of what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the religion of Islam. The introduction says the Holy Quran is the source of growth and guidance and the foundation of Islam. The whole religion stands upon the Quran and the Sunnah.

mcqs.q: Which paras are fixed for Nazra Quran in this class?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Para 7 to 12. The book fixes six paras, from Para 7 (Wa Idha Sami'u) to Para 12 (Wa Ma Min Da'bbah), for Nazra reading in Class 6. Students read them by looking at the Quran.

mcqs.q: How many paras in total have to be read in the Nazra part?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is six paras. Counting from Para 7 to Para 12 gives six paras in all. Each para also has its own name, taken from its opening words.

mcqs.q: Para 7 begins with which words?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Wa Idha Sami'u'. The seventh para starts with these words, and that is why this is also its name. In the same way, Para 8 is 'Wa Lau Annana' and Para 9 is 'Qalal Mala'u'.

mcqs.q: According to the book, how should the Nazra Quran be read?
options: With correct pronunciation and vowels, Qira'at and Tajweed, and in a pleasant voice
mcqs.why: The correct answer is with correct pronunciation and vowels, Qira'at and Tajweed, and in a pleasant voice. The book instructs that Nazra should also be fluent. Reading correctly is the first right of the Holy Quran.

mcqs.q: What total percentage of marks is fixed for the Nazra, Hifz and translation part?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 40 percent. The book states that forty percent of the marks of Islamiat are for this Quran part. Its marks are also written separately in the result sheet.

mcqs.q: What has been declared compulsory for passing the subject of Islamiat?
options: Passing the Nazra and Hifz part
mcqs.why: The correct answer is passing the Nazra and Hifz part. The book clearly says that success in this part is necessary for success in Islamiat. So a student must prepare the Quran part well.

mcqs.q: What does 'Nazra' mean?
options: Reading the Quran by looking at it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is reading the Quran by looking at it. 'Nazra' comes from looking, so reading while looking at the Holy Quran is called Nazra. Learning something by heart is called Hifz, which is different.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a right of the Holy Quran upon us?
options: Opening it only in difficult times
Keeping it only in a cupboard
Acting upon it and conveying its teachings to others
mcqs.why: The correct answer is acting upon it and conveying its teachings to others. The book lists four rights of the Quran: reciting it with Tajweed, pondering over it, acting upon it, and preaching its teachings. Merely keeping it at home is not its right.

lessons.title: Hifz Quran Majeed — Surah Al-Inshirah, Surah At-Tin, Surah Al-Qadr
lessons.notes_html:
What is Hifz?

Hifz means learning by heart (memorising). In this unit, three surahs are given to memorise with correct pronunciation and vowels:

  • Surah Al-Inshirah
  • Surah At-Tin
  • Surah Al-Qadr

Surah Al-Inshirah (8 Verses)

  • Allah Almighty opened the chest of His Prophet ﷺ.
  • He removed from him the burden that had broken his back.
  • He raised high the fame of the Prophet ﷺ.
  • The great good news of this surah is: surely, with every hardship there is ease.
  • At the end, the command is: when you are free, strive in worship, and turn to your Lord with devotion.

Surah At-Tin (8 Verses)

  • Allah Almighty swore by the fig and the olive, by Mount Sinai and by this city of peace (Makkah).
  • He said: We created man in the best form.
  • For those who believe and do good deeds, there is a reward that will never end.

Surah Al-Qadr (5 Verses)

  • The Holy Quran was revealed in Laylat-ul-Qadr (the Night of Decree).
  • Laylat-ul-Qadr is better than one thousand months.
  • In this night, the angels and the Spirit (Jibrail) descend by the command of their Lord for every matter.
  • This night is complete peace until the rising of dawn.

Activity

Students should memorise the Nazra Quran and the surahs given in the lesson and recite them to their classmates one by one. The teacher will keep guiding them and, at the end, will listen to the memorised verses himself.

mcqs.q: Which surahs are given for Hifz (memorising) in this class?
options: Surah Al-Feel, Surah Quraish, Surah Al-Ma'un
Surah Al-Fatihah, Surah Al-Baqarah, Surah Aal-e-Imran
Surah Al-Inshirah, Surah At-Tin, Surah Al-Qadr
Surah Yaseen, Surah Al-Mulk, Surah Al-Kahf
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Al-Inshirah, Surah At-Tin and Surah Al-Qadr. The book fixes exactly these three small surahs for memorisation in Class 6. They are to be learnt with correct pronunciation and vowels.

mcqs.q: How many verses are there in Surah Al-Inshirah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8 verses. Surah Al-Inshirah has eight verses in which Allah speaks of opening the chest of the Prophet ﷺ and raising his fame. Surah At-Tin also has 8 verses, while Surah Al-Qadr has 5.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Qadr, Laylat-ul-Qadr is better than what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one thousand months. Surah Al-Qadr itself says that the Night of Decree is better than a thousand months. In this night the Quran was revealed and the angels descend.

mcqs.q: What good news is given in Surah Al-Inshirah?
options: With every hardship there is ease
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: with every hardship there is ease. This is the famous promise of Surah Al-Inshirah, repeated for emphasis. It teaches a believer never to lose hope in difficulty.

mcqs.q: In Surah At-Tin, Allah Almighty swore by which things?
options: The fig and the olive, Mount Sinai and the city of peace
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the fig and the olive, Mount Sinai and the city of peace. After these oaths, Allah says He created man in the best form. The city of peace means Makkah Mukarramah.

mcqs.q: What has Allah said about man in Surah At-Tin?
options: Man was created only for play
Man was created from water only
Man was created in the best form
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that man was created in the best form. Surah At-Tin says Allah made the human being in the finest shape and form. For believers who do good deeds, there is never-ending reward.

mcqs.q: In which night was the Holy Quran revealed, according to Surah Al-Qadr?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Laylat-ul-Qadr. Surah Al-Qadr begins with the news that the Quran was sent down in this blessed night. It is the night in which angels descend with every matter by Allah's command.

mcqs.q: Who descends in Laylat-ul-Qadr?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the angels and the Spirit, Jibrail (AS). Surah Al-Qadr says they descend for every matter by the permission of their Lord. The whole night remains peace until dawn.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of 'Hifz'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is learning by heart. Hifz means to memorise something so that it can be recited without looking. Reading by looking at the Quran is called Nazra, not Hifz.

mcqs.q: How many verses are there in Surah Al-Qadr?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 5 verses. Surah Al-Qadr is a short surah of five verses, all about the greatness of Laylat-ul-Qadr. Surah Al-Inshirah and Surah At-Tin have 8 verses each.

lessons.title: Duaein — Hifz and Translation of Three Dua Verses
lessons.notes_html:
Dua Verses to Memorise with Translation

Three verses of dua are to be learnt by heart with their translation, so that we may pray to Allah Almighty in these very words.

1. Surah Al-Baqarah, Verse 250

Rabbana afrigh 'alayna sabran wa thabbit aqdamana wansurna 'alal-qawmil-kafirin.

Translation: "O our Lord! Pour patience upon us, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people."

2. Surah Al-A'raf, Verse 23

Rabbana zalamna anfusana wa illam taghfir lana wa tarhamna lanakunanna minal-khasirin.

Translation: "O our Lord! We have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we shall surely be among the losers."

3. Surah Al-Hashr, Verse 10

Rabbanaghfir lana wa li-ikhwaninalladhina sabaquna bil-iman wa la taj'al fi qulubina ghillal-lilladhina amanu, Rabbana innaka Ra'ufur-Rahim.

Translation: "O our Lord! Forgive us and our brothers who believed before us, and do not put any grudge in our hearts against the believers. O our Lord! Surely You are Most Kind, Most Merciful."

Remember

  • Write these duas beautifully with their translation and hang them at a prominent place; memorise them and recite them to one another.
  • The teacher will explain these duas briefly and will also make the students practise making dua practically.
  • Allah Almighty has said: "And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?" (Surah Al-Qamar, Verse 17)

mcqs.q: The dua 'Rabbana afrigh alayna sabran wa thabbit aqdamana' is a verse of which surah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Al-Baqarah. This dua is verse 250 of Surah Al-Baqarah, asking Allah for patience, firm feet and help. The book has fixed it for memorisation with translation.

mcqs.q: In the dua of Surah Al-A'raf (verse 23), what is asked from Allah Almighty?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is forgiveness and mercy. In this dua we confess that we have wronged ourselves and beg Allah to forgive us and have mercy on us. Without His forgiveness, we would be among the losers.

mcqs.q: In the dua of Surah Al-Hashr (verse 10), what is said about the believers?
options: That no grudge be put in our hearts against them
That we get more wealth than them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that no grudge be put in our hearts against them. This dua also asks forgiveness for ourselves and for the believers who came before us. It teaches love and brotherhood among Muslims.

mcqs.q: How many dua verses are fixed for Hifz and translation in this unit?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three verses. They are: Surah Al-Baqarah verse 250, Surah Al-A'raf verse 23 and Surah Al-Hashr verse 10. Each one is to be memorised together with its translation.

mcqs.q: The dua 'Rabbana zalamna anfusana' is from which surah and verse?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Al-A'raf, verse 23. In it, the words 'we have wronged ourselves' are used, and forgiveness is sought. Surah Al-Baqarah 250 is the dua for patience and firmness.

mcqs.q: What is asked for in the dua of Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 250?
options: Patience, firm feet and help against the disbelievers
mcqs.why: The correct answer is patience, firm feet and help against the disbelievers. The words 'afrigh alayna sabran' mean 'pour patience upon us'. This dua is made at the time of facing a great trial.

mcqs.q: What does Allah Almighty say in Surah Al-Qamar, verse 17, quoted in this lesson?
options: The Quran should not be translated
The Quran is only for the elders
The Quran is only for scholars
We have made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'We have made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?' This verse encourages every student to learn and remember the Quran. It is quoted at the end of this unit.

mcqs.q: For whom is forgiveness asked in the dua of Surah Al-Hashr?
options: For ourselves and for the believers who came before us
mcqs.why: The correct answer is for ourselves and for the believers who came before us. The dua says 'forgive us and our brothers who believed before us'. It teaches us to pray for all Muslims, not only for ourselves.

mcqs.q: What will the teacher do after making the students memorise these duas?
options: Explain them briefly and make the students practise making dua
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the teacher will explain them briefly and make the students practise making dua. The book directs the teacher to give a short explanation of the duas. The aim is that students actually use these words in their prayers.

mcqs.q: What activity is given in the book for these duas?
options: To write them beautifully with translation, display them, memorise them and recite them to one another
To keep them in a notebook unseen
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to write them beautifully with translation, display them, memorise them and recite them to one another. The book gives this activity so that the duas are remembered well. Learning them with translation is part of the task.

chapters.title: Imaniyat & Ibadat — Tauheed, Azan, Namaz, Hajj

lessons.title: Tauheed — Meaning and Concept
lessons.notes_html:
Faith in Allah Almighty

Having faith in the Being of Allah Almighty means keeping firmly in one's heart, with certainty, that:

  • Allah Almighty has always existed and will always remain; He has neither a beginning nor an end.
  • He is the Creator of the universe; He alone created this universe.
  • He is One and Unique in His Being and His attributes.
  • No one besides Him is worthy of worship.

Proof of the Existence of Allah

  • The sun, the moon and the stars revolve in their orbits at fixed times.
  • The coming of day and night, the changing of seasons and the falling of rain all happen in an organised manner and with regularity.
  • This shows that only One Being runs the system of this universe.
  • Even a small thing, like a needle, cannot exist without a maker — so how can this whole universe exist without a Maker? That Being is Allah Almighty.

If There Were More Than One God

If there had been another god besides Allah, the whole universe would have fallen into disorder and chaos. Allah Almighty says in the Holy Quran: "If there had been (many) gods in the heavens and the earth besides Allah, both would have been ruined." (Surah Al-Anbiya, Verse 22)

Requirements of Tauheed

  • To accept Allah Almighty alone as the Creator and Owner of the whole universe, without any partner.
  • To place complete trust in Allah Almighty.
  • To seek help from Him alone in all difficulties and troubles.
  • To prostrate before Him alone.

Results of Tauheed

  • Tauheed is the means of success in the Hereafter; without it, entering Paradise is impossible.
  • Tauheed is the source of all good deeds.
  • From a true believer in Tauheed come courage, bravery, patience, steadfastness, trust in Allah, and the fear of Allah.
  • The first of all beliefs is belief in the Being of Allah Almighty; the literal meaning of Tauheed is "to accept as One".
  • The basic points of Tauheed are stated in Surah Al-Ikhlas; the belief given the most importance in Islam is the belief of Tauheed.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Tauheed?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'to accept as One'. Tauheed means believing that Allah Almighty is One in His Being and attributes. The book's own exercise gives this as the literal meaning of Tauheed.

mcqs.q: Which is the first of all beliefs?
options: Belief in the Day of Judgement
Belief in the Being of Allah Almighty
Belief in the prophethood of the Messengers
mcqs.why: The correct answer is belief in the Being of Allah Almighty. The book's exercise states this is the first belief, before all others. Every other belief is built upon faith in Allah.

mcqs.q: In which Surah of the Holy Quran are the basic points of Tauheed stated?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Al-Ikhlas. This short surah purely describes the Oneness of Allah: He is One, He needs no one, and there is none like Him. The book's exercise names it for the basic points of Tauheed.

mcqs.q: Entering Paradise without Tauheed is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is impossible. The lesson says Tauheed is the means of success in the Hereafter, and without Tauheed entering Paradise is impossible. That is why Tauheed is the source of all good deeds.

mcqs.q: What would have happened if there had been more than one god?
options: People would have had more choices
The universe would have run better
The universe would have fallen into disorder and chaos
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the universe would have fallen into disorder and chaos. The lesson explains that one god would order the sun from one side and another from the other side. Surah Al-Anbiya (22) says heaven and earth would have been ruined.

mcqs.q: Which argument does the lesson give for the existence of Allah Almighty?
options: Even a needle cannot exist without a maker, so the universe must also have a Maker
It is written in history books only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the needle argument. The lesson says that when even a tiny needle cannot exist without a craftsman, this vast universe cannot exist without a Maker. The regular movement of the sun, moon and stars points to the same One Being.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a requirement of Tauheed?
options: To seek help from saints in trouble
To seek help from Allah alone in all difficulties
To trust only in one's wealth
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to seek help from Allah alone in all difficulties. The requirements of Tauheed include accepting Allah alone as Creator and Owner and prostrating before Him alone. Seeking help from others in the sense of worship is against Tauheed.

mcqs.q: The basic purpose of the preaching of all the Prophets and Messengers was to give the teaching of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the belief of Tauheed. The book's fill-in exercise says every Prophet who came into this world taught Tauheed first of all. It is the common message of all the Messengers.

mcqs.q: Through Tauheed, a person is saved from:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is hypocrisy. The book's exercise says that through Tauheed a person is saved from hypocrisy, because his belief becomes pure and sincere. Tauheed also fills a believer with courage, patience and trust in Allah.

mcqs.q: Which belief has been given the most importance in Islam?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the belief of Tauheed. The book states that the belief whose importance has been emphasised most of all in Islam is Tauheed. It is the foundation on which the whole religion stands.

lessons.title: Adhan — Virtue and Importance
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Adhan

  • The literal meaning of Adhan is "to announce" or "to call".
  • The Adhan is a cause of preparation for Salah: through it, people learn that the time of congregational Salah has come.
  • After hearing the Adhan, a desire arises in Muslims to go to the mosque, offer Salah in congregation, earn its reward, and meet one another.
  • The Adhan is given five times in a day and night, and it began in Madinah Munawwarah after the Hijrah.

Virtue of the Adhan and the Mu'adhdhin

  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said that if people knew the reward of giving the Adhan and of standing in the first row, they would even draw lots for it.
  • On the Day of Judgement, the necks of the Mu'adhdhins will be raised high.
  • At the time of the Adhan, Satan goes far away where the sound of the Adhan cannot be heard.
  • As far as the sound of the Adhan reaches, the jinn and humans there will bear witness for the Mu'adhdhin on the Day of Judgement.
  • Whoever gives the Adhan for seven years with the intention of reward, deliverance from the Fire will be written for him.
  • The Mu'adhdhin is called the "Ameen" (trustee) of the Muslims; the first Mu'adhdhin of Islam was Hazrat Bilal (RA).
  • The words of the Adhan were taught to the Holy Prophet ﷺ through revelation; at its beginning, the greatness of Allah Almighty is proclaimed.

Special Words of the Fajr Adhan

In the Adhan of Fajr, after "Hayya 'alal-Falah", the words "As-Salatu khairum-minan-naum" are said, which mean: "Salah is better than sleep."

Etiquettes of the Adhan

  • Remain silent at the time of the Adhan and listen to it attentively, reflecting upon its words.
  • Repeat the words of the Mu'adhdhin; but at "Hayya 'alas-Salah" and "Hayya 'alal-Falah", say "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah".
  • After the Adhan, recite the dua "Allahumma Rabba hadhihid-da'wah...".
  • After the birth of a child, the Adhan is said in his right ear and the Iqamah in his left ear.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Adhan?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'to announce or to call'. The Adhan announces that the time of Salah has come and calls the Muslims to the mosque. This is the literal meaning given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: How many times is the Adhan given in a day and night?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is five times. There are five daily prayers, and the Adhan is called before each one. The book's fill-in exercise gives this number.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Mu'adhdhin of Islam?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Bilal (RA). The book's true/false exercise corrects the statement about Abu Mahdhurah and confirms Hazrat Bilal (RA) as the first Mu'adhdhin. He was appointed by the Holy Prophet ﷺ himself.

mcqs.q: Where did the Adhan begin?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Madinah Munawwarah. The book states that the Adhan began in Madinah after the Hijrah, not in Makkah. There the Muslims first gathered for congregational prayers.

mcqs.q: In the Adhan of which Salah are the words 'As-Salatu khairum-minan-naum' said?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Fajr. Only in the Fajr Adhan, after 'Hayya alal-Falah', are the words 'Salah is better than sleep' added. This is because Fajr comes at the time of sleep.

mcqs.q: What do the words 'As-Salatu khairum-minan-naum' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Salah is better than sleep'. The lesson gives this translation of the Arabic words added in the Fajr Adhan. It reminds the sleeper that prayer brings more benefit than sleep.

mcqs.q: What should a listener say when the Mu'adhdhin says 'Hayya alas-Salah' and 'Hayya alal-Falah'?
options: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah'. The lesson's etiquettes say the listener repeats the Mu'adhdhin's words, except at these two calls, where this phrase is said. All other words are repeated.

mcqs.q: What will happen to the Mu'adhdhins on the Day of Judgement?
options: Their necks will be raised high
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that their necks will be raised high. The lesson quotes the Ahadith that on the Day of Judgement the Mu'adhdhins' necks will be long and raised. This is a sign of their honour.

mcqs.q: After the birth of a child, what is said in his right ear?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Adhan. The book's exercise says that after birth, first of all the Adhan is said in the child's right ear and the Iqamah in his left ear. Thus the first words a Muslim hears are the words of the Adhan.

mcqs.q: The Mu'adhdhin has been called what of the Muslims?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Ameen' (trustee). The book's true/false exercise confirms that the Mu'adhdhin is called the trustee of the Muslims. People trust his call for the times of prayer and fasting.

lessons.title: Salah — Importance, Virtue and its Fard
lessons.notes_html:
Importance of Salah

  • Allah Almighty has stated worship as the purpose of the creation of humans and jinn.
  • The Holy Quran has described Salah as a means of protection from evils: "Indeed, Salah restrains from indecency and evil deeds." (Surah Al-Ankabut, Verse 45)
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "Salah is the pillar of the religion."
  • Salah is an important means of attaining the nearness of Allah Almighty, and it makes the bond between a servant and his Lord strong.
  • A person offering Salah expresses supplication and humility before Allah Almighty.
  • On the Day of Judgement, the first questioning will be about Salah.
  • In the Holy Quran, at various places, great emphasis has been laid on offering Salah.

Good Habits from Salah

  • Punctuality and discipline.
  • Forming rows, obedience to the Imam.
  • Equality, love and brotherhood.
  • Remaining clean and pure, and speaking the truth.

The Seven Fard of Salah

There are 7 Fard (obligatory acts) inside Salah:

  • (1) Takbir-e-Tahrimah — beginning Salah by saying "Allahu Akbar".
  • (2) Qiyam — standing.
  • (3) Qira'at — recitation.
  • (4) Ruku — bowing.
  • (5) Sajdah — prostration.
  • (6) The last Qa'dah — sitting at the end.
  • (7) Completing Salah with Salam.

Remember

  • Some conditions of Salah must be fulfilled before it, and the Fard listed above are inside Salah and must be fulfilled.
  • Salah offered after its time has passed is called Qada; Salah offered at its own time is not Qada.

mcqs.q: The Holy Prophet ﷺ described Salah as what of the religion?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Pillar of the religion'. This is the Hadith quoted in the lesson: 'Salah is the pillar of the religion.' Just as a building stands on pillars, the religion stands firm through Salah.

mcqs.q: What purpose of the creation of humans and jinn has the Holy Quran stated?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is worship. The lesson says Allah Almighty has stated worship as the purpose of creating humans and jinn. Salah is the greatest form of that worship.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Ankabut (45), Salah restrains a person from what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is indecency and evil deeds. The verse quoted in the lesson says: 'Indeed, Salah restrains from indecency and evil deeds.' Regular prayer keeps a person away from sins.

mcqs.q: How many Fard are there in Salah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 7. The lesson lists seven Fard inside Salah, from Takbir-e-Tahrimah to ending with Salam. If any one of them is left out, the Salah is not valid.

mcqs.q: What is the status of Ruku in Salah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Fard. Ruku (bowing) is one of the seven Fard inside Salah, like Qiyam, Qira'at and Sajdah. The book's own MCQ exercise confirms this.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven Fard of Salah?
options: Raising the hands at every step
mcqs.why: The correct answer is raising the hands at every step — it is not in the list. The seven Fard are: Takbir-e-Tahrimah, Qiyam, Qira'at, Ruku, Sajdah, the last Qa'dah, and completing with Salam.

mcqs.q: On the Day of Judgement, the first questioning will be about what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Salah. The lesson states that on the Day of Judgement the first thing about which questioning will take place will be Salah. This shows its supreme importance among deeds.

mcqs.q: Salah offered after its time has passed is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Qada. The lesson's fill-in exercise says that Salah offered after its time is called Qada. Salah offered at its own time is called Ada, not Qada.

mcqs.q: A person offering Salah expresses what before Allah Almighty?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is supplication and humility. The lesson says that in Salah a person presents his dua and humility before his Lord. Pride has no place in prayer.

mcqs.q: Salah makes the bond between a servant and his Lord:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is strong. The lesson's matching exercise confirms that Salah makes the bond between the servant and Allah strong. It is an important means of attaining Allah's nearness.

mcqs.q: Which good habits does a person learn from offering Salah?
options: Punctuality, discipline, equality, love and brotherhood
mcqs.why: The correct answer is punctuality, discipline, equality, love and brotherhood. The lesson lists these habits: standing in rows, obeying the Imam, and remaining clean and truthful. Salah trains a person's whole character.

mcqs.q: What is Takbir-e-Tahrimah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is beginning Salah by saying 'Allahu Akbar'. It is the first of the seven Fard. With this Takbir, worldly talk and actions become forbidden (haram) during the prayer — hence the name Tahrimah.

mcqs.q: What is the last of the seven Fard of Salah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is completing Salah with Salam. The list of Fard ends with turning the Salam, after the last Qa'dah. Ruku, Sajdah and Qira'at come earlier in the prayer.

mcqs.q: Where has great emphasis been laid on offering Salah?
options: In the Holy Quran at various places
mcqs.why: The correct answer is in the Holy Quran at various places. The lesson's matching exercise states this fact. Again and again, the Quran commands the believers to establish Salah.

mcqs.q: The Fard of Salah are located where?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is inside Salah. The lesson distinguishes the conditions, which are fulfilled before Salah, from the seven Fard, which are performed inside the prayer itself. Both must be fulfilled for a valid Salah.

lessons.title: Namaz-e-Janaza (Funeral Prayer) and its Importance
lessons.notes_html:
What is Fard-e-Kifayah?

The funeral prayer (Namaz-e-Janaza) is Fard-e-Kifayah. It means: if some people of the area where a person has died offer the funeral prayer, it is counted as offered on behalf of the whole area. But if no one at all offers it, all the people of that village or area become sinners.

Method of the Funeral Prayer

  • First of all, the deceased is given a bath (ghusl), then dressed in the shroud (kafan).
  • Close relatives carry the deceased on a cot on their shoulders.
  • The Muslims of the area gather at an open place and form rows; the deceased is placed in front.
  • The Imam stands in front, and the people stand in rows behind him.
  • The Imam says four additional Takbirs; the praise of Allah, Durood upon the Holy Prophet ﷺ, and the dua for the forgiveness of the deceased are recited.
  • Finally, the prayer is completed by turning the Salam.
  • In the funeral prayer, there is neither Ruku nor Sajdah.

Lessons of the Funeral Prayer

  • Allah Almighty says: "Every soul is to taste death." (Surah Al-Ankabut, Verse 57)
  • In reality, the funeral prayer is a supplication for the forgiveness of the deceased.
  • It gives the one who offers it the feeling of the impermanence of this world — he too must leave one day, so he tries to reform his deeds and character.
  • In Islam, the deceased is buried in a most dignified manner.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ himself used to take part in the funeral prayer and instructed people to definitely take part in it.

mcqs.q: What is the status of the funeral prayer for Muslims?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Fard-e-Kifayah. The lesson explains that if some people of the area offer it, it counts for everyone, but if nobody offers it, all become sinners. That is exactly the meaning of Fard-e-Kifayah.

mcqs.q: What is the very first act performed for the deceased before burial?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is giving a bath. The lesson's method begins: first the deceased is given ghusl, then dressed in the kafan (shroud). Only after that is the funeral prayer offered.

mcqs.q: In the funeral prayer, there are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is neither Ruku nor Sajdah. The funeral prayer is offered standing, with four Takbirs, praise, Durood and dua. The book's MCQ and fill-in exercises both confirm this.

mcqs.q: How many additional Takbirs does the Imam say in the funeral prayer?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is four. The lesson's method states that the Imam says four additional Takbirs, between which praise of Allah, Durood and the dua for the deceased are recited. The prayer ends with Salam.

mcqs.q: In reality, the funeral prayer is what for the deceased?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a supplication for forgiveness. The lesson says the funeral prayer is, in reality, a dua to Allah for the forgiveness of the deceased. That is its true purpose.

mcqs.q: What has Allah Almighty said about death in the Holy Quran, as quoted in the lesson?
options: Death is the end of everything
Death comes only to the old
Every soul is to taste death
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Every soul is to taste death'. This is Surah Al-Ankabut, verse 57, quoted in the lesson. It reminds every living person that death will surely come.

mcqs.q: What feeling does the funeral prayer give to the one who offers it?
options: The feeling of the impermanence of this world
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the feeling of the impermanence of this world. The lesson says the worshipper realises that he too must leave this mortal world one day. So he tries to reform his deeds and character.

mcqs.q: If no one in an area offers the funeral prayer of a deceased person, then:
options: All the people of that area become sinners
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that all the people of that area become sinners. This is the ruling of Fard-e-Kifayah explained in the lesson. If some people offer it, the duty is discharged for all.

mcqs.q: How is the deceased buried in Islam?
options: In a simple pit without care
mcqs.why: The correct answer is in a most dignified manner. The lesson's fill-in exercise says Islam buries the deceased with full honour and dignity. Respect for the dead body is part of our faith.

mcqs.q: Who himself used to take part in the funeral prayer and instructed others to do so?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Holy Prophet ﷺ. The lesson's matching exercise says he himself used to take part in the funeral prayer. He also instructed people to definitely participate in it.

lessons.title: Hajj and its Importance
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and Importance of Hajj

  • The literal meaning of Hajj is "to intend to visit".
  • In Islam, Hajj means going with the intention of worship to perform Tawaf of Baitullah (the Holy Ka'bah) and to be present at the sacred places, performing the specific acts and etiquettes.
  • Hajj is a most important pillar of Islam — the fifth pillar.
  • Hajj is obligatory upon every sane, adult and healthy Muslim who has the ability (means) to perform it; it became obligatory in 9 AH.
  • Hajj is both a physical and a financial act of worship.
  • In reality, Hajj is the Sunnah of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), and it is a memorial of the great sacrifices of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), Hazrat Bibi Hajra (RA) and Hazrat Ismail (AS).
  • After Hajj became obligatory, the Holy Prophet ﷺ performed Hajj once in his life, famous as "Hajjat-ul-Wida" (the Farewell Hajj).

The Days and Rites of Hajj

  • The rites of Hajj begin with the stay at Mina on the morning of 8th Dhul-Hijjah.
  • On 9th Dhul-Hijjah, Wuquf (stay) is observed in the plain of Arafat.
  • Then comes the stay in the valley of Muzdalifah on the night of 10th Dhul-Hijjah.
  • After that: Rami al-Jimar (throwing stones), sacrifice, Halq or Qasr (shaving or shortening the hair), and finally Tawaf-e-Ziyarah of Baitullah — without which Hajj is not complete.
  • At Mina, stones are thrown at Satan seven times seven; this act is called Rami al-Jimar.
  • Sa'i means running between Safa and Marwah, which are near Baitullah.

Benefits of Hajj

  • The greatest benefit of Hajj is to obtain the pleasure of Allah Almighty and His nearness, and the forgiveness of sins.
  • Through Hajj, purification from sins and piety in faith are attained.
  • There is also an economic benefit: pilgrims from different countries gain countless trade benefits through mutual exchange and trade.

mcqs.q: Safa and Marwah are located near:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Baitullah. The lesson's MCQ exercise confirms that Safa and Marwah are near the Holy Ka'bah in Makkah. The Sa'i between them is part of Hajj and Umrah.

mcqs.q: In which year did Hajj become obligatory?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 9 AH. The book's exercise gives this year for Hajj becoming obligatory. After that, the Holy Prophet ﷺ performed his one Hajj, known as Hajjat-ul-Wida.

mcqs.q: Hajj is obligatory upon:
options: Both the poor and the rich
Those who have the ability to perform Hajj
mcqs.why: The correct answer is those who have the ability to perform Hajj. The lesson says Hajj is Fard on every sane, adult and healthy Muslim who has the means for the journey. A person without the ability is not bound by it.

mcqs.q: How many times did the Holy Prophet ﷺ perform Hajj after it became obligatory?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is once. The lesson states that the Holy Prophet ﷺ performed Hajj one time in his life. That Hajj is famous by the name Hajjat-ul-Wida, the Farewell Hajj.

mcqs.q: The pilgrims observe Wuquf (the great stay) at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Arafat. On 9th Dhul-Hijjah, Wuquf is observed in the plain of Arafat; it is the greatest rite of Hajj. Mina is the place of stay on the 8th and of Rami, not of Wuquf.

mcqs.q: Hajj is which pillar of Islam?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the fifth pillar. The lesson and its fill-in exercise both call Hajj the fifth important pillar of Islam. It comes after Shahadah, Salah, Zakat and fasting.

mcqs.q: What does Sa'i mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is running between Safa and Marwah. The lesson's fill-in exercise gives this meaning of Sa'i. Circling the Ka'bah is called Tawaf, and throwing stones is Rami al-Jimar.

mcqs.q: Throwing stones at Mina is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Rami al-Jimar. The lesson says that at Mina, stones are thrown at Satan seven times seven, and this act is called Rami al-Jimar. It is one of the rites performed after Muzdalifah.

mcqs.q: Hajj is a memorial of the sacrifices of whom?
options: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), Hazrat Bibi Hajra (RA) and Hazrat Ismail (AS)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), Hazrat Bibi Hajra (RA) and Hazrat Ismail (AS). The lesson calls Hajj a memorial of their great sacrifices. The lesson also says Hajj is, in reality, the Sunnah of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).

mcqs.q: On which date do the rites of Hajj begin with the stay at Mina?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8th Dhul-Hijjah. The lesson says the rites begin with staying at Mina on the morning of the 8th. The 9th is the day of Wuquf at Arafat, and the night of the 10th is spent at Muzdalifah.
