lessons.title: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (Sulah Hudaybiyyah)
lessons.notes_html:
The Dream and the Journey

  • In the sixth year of the Hijrah (6 AH), the Holy Prophet ﷺ saw a dream that he had reached Makkah Mukarramah with the noble Companions (RA) and performed Umrah.
  • The Prophet ﷺ was going to Makkah for Umrah — not for war or trade.
  • About 12 kilometres from Madinah is a place called Dhul-Hulayfah; there the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions made the intention for Umrah and put on the Ihram.
  • Hudaybiyyah is at a distance of about 10 miles from Makkah Mukarramah.
  • The Prophet ﷺ sent Hazrat Busr bin Sufyan (RA) to find out the conditions of the people of Makkah.

Bay'at-e-Ridwan

  • The Prophet ﷺ made Hazrat Usman (RA) his special envoy and sent him to the Quraysh for negotiations.
  • When Hazrat Usman (RA) was delayed, a rumour spread that he had been martyred; this was the real cause of Bay'at-e-Ridwan.
  • The pledge was taken under a babool tree, where the Prophet ﷺ sat and took the pledge from the Companions.

Conditions of the Treaty

  • The Muslims and the Quraysh would be bound not to fight for ten years.
  • This year the Muslims would return without performing Umrah; permission would be given only for Umrah next year.
  • If any person from the Quraysh became a Muslim and came to Madinah, the Muslims would be bound to return him; but if any Muslim went to the Quraysh, the Quraysh would not return him.
  • These conditions were apparently against the Muslims.

Results of the Treaty

  • In the Holy Quran, this treaty has been called "Fath-e-Mubeen" — a clear victory: "Indeed, We have given you a clear victory." (Al-Fath: 1)
  • The status of the Muslims was recognised.
  • Trade caravans began to move freely.
  • The polytheists got the opportunity to judge the reality of Islam by contact with the sincerity, good deeds and pure character of the Muslims.
  • This treaty later became the cause of the Conquest of Makkah.

mcqs.q: In which year of the Hijrah did the Prophet ﷺ see the dream of performing Umrah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 6 AH. The lesson says that in the sixth year of the Hijrah the Prophet ﷺ saw in a dream that he had reached Makkah with the Companions and performed Umrah. On this dream the journey to Makkah was made.

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ was travelling to Makkah Mukarramah for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Umrah. The Muslims carried no intention of fighting; they wore Ihram for Umrah. The book's MCQ exercise confirms this purpose of the journey.

mcqs.q: What was the real cause of Bay'at-e-Ridwan?
options: The rumour of the martyrdom of Hazrat Usman (RA)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the rumour of the martyrdom of Hazrat Usman (RA). He had been sent as an envoy and was delayed, so the false news spread. The Muslims then pledged, under a tree, to stand firm.

mcqs.q: Under which tree did the Prophet ﷺ sit and take the pledge (Bay'at)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the babool tree. The book's MCQ exercise names the babool as the tree under which Bay'at-e-Ridwan took place. This pledge was taken at Hudaybiyyah.

mcqs.q: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ send to find out the conditions of the people of Makkah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Busr bin Sufyan (RA). The book's exercise names him as the Companion sent ahead to learn the situation in Makkah. Hazrat Usman (RA) was later sent as the special envoy for negotiations.

mcqs.q: For how many years were the Muslims and the Quraysh bound not to fight, under the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ten years. The fill-in exercise states that both sides were bound to peace for ten years. This peace gave Islam the chance to spread without war.

mcqs.q: In the Holy Quran, the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah has been called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Fath-e-Mubeen, a clear victory. Surah Al-Fath (verse 1) says: 'Indeed, We have given you a clear victory.' Although its conditions seemed against the Muslims, Allah declared it a victory.

mcqs.q: The conditions of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah were apparently against:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Muslims. Returning without Umrah and returning any new Muslim to the Quraysh seemed one-sided. Yet the lesson shows the treaty later became the cause of the Conquest of Makkah.

mcqs.q: At which place did the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions put on the Ihram for Umrah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Dhul-Hulayfah, about 12 kilometres from Madinah. There the Prophet ﷺ and the noble Companions made the intention for Umrah and wore the Ihram. Hudaybiyyah was the halting place near Makkah.

mcqs.q: Which of these was a result of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
options: The status of the Muslims was recognised
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the status of the Muslims was recognised. The lesson lists this among the results, along with free movement of trade caravans. The treaty also later became the cause of the Conquest of Makkah.

lessons.title: Invitation of Islam to the Kings
lessons.notes_html:
Letters to the Kings

  • The writing of letters to kings began at the end of 6 AH.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ wrote letters inviting the kings of the world to Islam.
  • Three of the kings were: Najashi (king of Abyssinia), Mundhir bin Sawi (king of Bahrain), and Khusrau Parvez (king of Persia/Iran).
  • The king of Persia was called Kisra, the king of Rome was called Qaisar, and Heraclius was the king of Rome.
  • Bahrain was a small state in the region of Arabia.

The Envoys

  • Hazrat Amr bin Umayyah (RA) was sent with the letter to the king of Abyssinia.
  • Hazrat Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah (RA) carried the letter to Muqawqis, the king of Egypt.

Responses of the Kings

  • Najashi of Abyssinia: after reading the letter, he stood up out of respect, placed the blessed letter on his eyes, bore witness to the Oneness of Allah and the Prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, and embraced Islam.
  • Mundhir bin Sawi of Bahrain also accepted Islam after reading the blessed letter.
  • Muqawqis of Egypt showed great respect and sent valuable gifts: one white mule, one Abyssinian slave, and two Egyptian gifts named "Mariah" and "Sireen".
  • Khusrau Parvez of Persia became enraged, tore up the blessed letter, and objected that the Prophet ﷺ had written his own name above his name. The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah Almighty tear his kingdom to pieces." His son Sheroyah revolted, killed him and became king himself.

mcqs.q: The writing of letters to kings began at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the end of 6 AH. The book's MCQ exercise gives this time for the start of the letters to kings. This was after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah had brought peace.

mcqs.q: Which kings accepted Islam after reading the blessed letter of the Prophet ﷺ?
options: Najashi of Abyssinia and Mundhir bin Sawi of Bahrain
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Najashi of Abyssinia and Mundhir bin Sawi of Bahrain. The lesson says both of them accepted Islam after reading the letter. Khusrau Parvez, by contrast, tore the letter in anger.

mcqs.q: What did Najashi do when he read the letter of the Prophet ﷺ?
options: He stood up in respect, placed the letter on his eyes and embraced Islam
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he stood up in respect, placed the letter on his eyes and embraced Islam. The lesson says Najashi bore witness to Allah's Oneness and the Prophethood. His respect was the opposite of Khusrau Parvez's arrogance.

mcqs.q: Khusrau Parvez was killed by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his son. The lesson tells that his son Sheroyah revolted, killed Khusrau Parvez and became king himself. This fulfilled the Prophet's ﷺ words that Allah would tear his kingdom to pieces.

mcqs.q: Heraclius was the king of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Rome. The lesson states that Heraclius was the Roman king, who was called Qaisar. Egypt's king was Muqawqis and Persia's was Khusrau Parvez (Kisra).

mcqs.q: Hazrat Amr bin Umayyah (RA) was sent with a letter to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the king of Abyssinia. The book's exercise confirms Hazrat Amr bin Umayyah (RA) carried the letter to Najashi. The letter to Egypt went through Hazrat Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah (RA).

mcqs.q: What gifts did Muqawqis, the king of Egypt, send for the Prophet ﷺ?
options: A white mule, an Abyssinian slave, and two gifts named Mariah and Sireen
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a white mule, an Abyssinian slave, and two Egyptian gifts named Mariah and Sireen. The lesson lists these gifts sent by Muqawqis. He showed great respect for the letter, though he did not accept Islam.

mcqs.q: The king of Abyssinia was called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Najashi. The fill-in exercise gives this title for the Abyssinian king. Kisra was the title of Persia's king and Qaisar of Rome's king.

mcqs.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when Khusrau Parvez tore up his blessed letter?
options: May Allah tear his kingdom to pieces
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'May Allah tear his kingdom to pieces.' The lesson says this saying proved true when his own son killed him and took the kingdom. Arrogance towards the Prophet's ﷺ letter brought his ruin.

mcqs.q: Through whom did the Prophet ﷺ send the blessed letter to Muqawqis of Egypt?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah (RA). The fill-in exercise names him as the envoy to Egypt. Hazrat Amr bin Umayyah (RA) was the envoy to Abyssinia.

lessons.title: Ghazwa-e-Khyber
lessons.notes_html:
Why the Battle of Khaybar Took Place

  • The tribe of Banu Nadir had been expelled from Madinah because of its anti-Islam conspiracies; it went to Khaybar, took refuge there and made it its centre.
  • Near Khaybar, another tribe called Banu Ghatfan was also settled.
  • The Prophet ﷺ sent Hazrat Abdullah bin Rawahah (RA) to Khaybar to investigate; he confirmed the conspiracies of the Jews.
  • When the conspiracies were confirmed, the Prophet ﷺ announced Jihad against the people of Khaybar.

The Battle

  • The Prophet ﷺ set out for the Battle of Khaybar in Muharram 7 AH, after returning from Hudaybiyyah and staying in Madinah for the whole month of Dhul-Hijjah and some days of Muharram.
  • Khaybar is to the north of Madinah at a distance of 200 kilometres.
  • The Prophet ﷺ stayed in the valley of Wadi Rajee.
  • The Jews had a total of 8 forts; the first attack was made on the Naim fort.
  • The largest and strongest fort of the Jews was "Qamus", where brave champion warriors and great chiefs lived.
  • Abdullah bin Ubayy is called Raees-ul-Munafiqeen (chief of the hypocrites).

Hazrat Ali (RA) and Marhab

  • When Hazrat Ali's (RA) eyes were hurting, the Prophet ﷺ put his blessed saliva in his eyes (and they were cured).
  • Hazrat Ali (RA) first invited Marhab to Islam; Marhab rejected it with arrogance and came forward reciting verses of pride.
  • Hazrat Ali (RA) answered with verses beginning: "I am the one whose mother named me Haiderah (the lion)..." and defeated Marhab.

Lesson of Khaybar

Rebelling against Allah Almighty and His Messenger ﷺ and plotting against them brings disgrace and humiliation in this world and the Hereafter, because honour and dominance belong only to Allah and His Messenger. We should always strive to obey Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

mcqs.q: Khaybar is to the north of Madinah at a distance of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 200 kilometres. The book's MCQ exercise gives this distance for Khaybar, north of Madinah. It was a strong centre of the Jewish tribes.

mcqs.q: In which month and year did the Prophet ﷺ set out for the Battle of Khaybar?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Muharram 7 AH. The fill-in exercise states the Prophet ﷺ set out in Muharram of the seventh year. This was shortly after returning from Hudaybiyyah.

mcqs.q: Why had the tribe of Banu Nadir made Khaybar its centre?
options: After being expelled from Madinah for anti-Islam conspiracies
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they were expelled from Madinah for anti-Islam conspiracies. The lesson says Banu Nadir then took refuge in Khaybar and made it their centre. From there they continued plotting against Islam.

mcqs.q: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ send to Khaybar to investigate the conspiracies?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Abdullah bin Rawahah (RA). The lesson says he investigated and confirmed the conspiracies. Only then did the Prophet ﷺ announce Jihad against Khaybar.

mcqs.q: Which was the largest and strongest fort of the Jews at Khaybar?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Qamus. The lesson calls it the largest and strongest fort, where brave champion warriors and great chiefs lived. The first attack, however, was made on the Naim fort.

mcqs.q: How many forts did the Jews have at Khaybar in total?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8 forts. The fill-in exercise gives this total. These forts made Khaybar a very strong stronghold.

mcqs.q: When Hazrat Ali's (RA) eyes were hurting, what did the Prophet ﷺ put in his eyes?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his blessed saliva. The book's MCQ exercise states this, and his eyes were cured. Hazrat Ali (RA) then went forward and defeated the champion Marhab.

mcqs.q: Abdullah bin Ubayy is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Raees-ul-Munafiqeen, the chief of the hypocrites. The fill-in exercise gives this title for Abdullah bin Ubayy. He outwardly claimed Islam but inwardly opposed it.

mcqs.q: In which valley did the Prophet ﷺ stay during the Khaybar expedition?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Wadi Rajee. The book's MCQ exercise names this valley as the Prophet's ﷺ halting place. From there the attacks on the forts were organised.

mcqs.q: What lesson do we learn from the Battle of Khaybar?
options: Rebelling against Allah and His Messenger brings disgrace in both worlds
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that rebelling against Allah and His Messenger brings disgrace in both worlds. The lesson concludes that honour and dominance belong only to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. So we should always obey them.

chapters.title: Akhlaq & Adab — Taharat, Sadaqat, Amanat, Huqooq-ul-Ibad

lessons.title: Taharat — Cleanliness and Purity
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Taharat

  • Taharah means becoming free from impurity and filth; in Arabic, the word opposite to Taharah is Najasat (impurity).
  • Taharah means cleanliness of every kind: cleanliness of the body, clothing, speech, thought, ideas and the surrounding environment.

Importance of Cleanliness in Islam

  • In Islam, emphasis has been laid on cleanliness and purity at every step.
  • Allah Almighty loves cleanliness and purity: "And Allah loves those who keep themselves clean." (At-Tawbah, Ayah 108)
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "Cleanliness (purity) is a part of faith."
  • Our beloved Prophet ﷺ was an excellent model in adopting cleanliness, and he commanded his Ummah to adopt cleanliness.
  • By acting upon Islam's principles of cleanliness, we can lay the foundation of a high and ideal society.
  • Keeping clothing, home and neighbourhood free from filth is our duty; clothing is a person's mirror.
  • The success of an important worship like Salah depends on Taharah and cleanliness.
  • For the person who walks to the mosque in the state of Wudu, the angels pray (make dua).

Guiding Principles of Cleanliness

  • Remain physically clean and pure.
  • Clothing should be clean, neat and pure.
  • Use the Miswak for cleaning the mouth and teeth — using the Miswak is a cause of cleanliness of the mouth and the pleasure of the Lord.

Benefits of Cleanliness

  • By adopting Taharah and cleanliness, a person is saved from many diseases.
  • By adopting Taharah and cleanliness, a person becomes beloved of Allah Almighty.
  • We should all take special care of Taharah and cleanliness.

mcqs.q: By adopting Taharah and cleanliness, a person is saved from:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is diseases. The lesson lists this as a benefit of cleanliness: a clean person is saved from many diseases. Cleanliness also makes a person beloved of Allah.

mcqs.q: The Miswak cleans:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the mouth and teeth. The lesson says the Miswak is used for cleaning the mouth and teeth. It is also a cause of the pleasure of the Lord.

mcqs.q: Regarding Taharah and cleanliness, we should all:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is take special care. The lesson's MCQ exercise gives this as our duty towards cleanliness. Islam has emphasised cleanliness at every step.

mcqs.q: For the person who walks to the mosque in the state of Wudu, dua is made by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is angels. The book's exercise states that angels pray for the one who walks to the mosque with Wudu. This shows the reward of purity combined with prayer.

mcqs.q: Which Hadith is about Taharah and cleanliness?
options: La imana liman la amanata lahu
La dina liman la ahda lahu
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'At-Tuhuru shatrul-Iman' — cleanliness is a part of faith. This is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ quoted in the lesson. The other sayings are about intention, trust and promises.

mcqs.q: In Arabic, which word is used as the opposite of Taharah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Najasat. The fill-in exercise says Najasat (impurity and filth) is the opposite of Taharah. Taharah means becoming free from exactly that impurity.

mcqs.q: By Taharah is meant cleanliness of:
options: Every kind — body, clothing, speech, thought and environment
mcqs.why: The correct answer is cleanliness of every kind. The lesson defines Taharah broadly: body, clothing, speech, thought, ideas and surroundings. It is not limited to washing the body.

mcqs.q: In Islam, emphasis has been laid on cleanliness:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is at every step. The fill-in exercise uses exactly these words. Cleanliness in Islam is a daily, all-time duty, not an occasional one.

mcqs.q: Our beloved Prophet ﷺ was what, in adopting cleanliness?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an excellent model. The lesson says the Prophet ﷺ himself practised cleanliness perfectly and commanded his Ummah to adopt it. We follow his example in purity.

mcqs.q: Clothing is a person's:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is mirror. The matching exercise says clothing reflects a person like a mirror. That is why clothing should be clean, neat and pure.

mcqs.q: The success of which important worship depends on Taharah and cleanliness?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Salah. The true/false exercise confirms that the success of Salah depends on Taharah. Without purity and Wudu, prayer cannot be offered properly.

mcqs.q: Keeping clothing, home and neighbourhood free from filth is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is our duty. The lesson's true/false exercise marks this statement correct. Cleanliness of surroundings is every Muslim's responsibility.

mcqs.q: Allah Almighty loves those who:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is those who keep themselves clean. The lesson quotes the Quran (At-Tawbah: 108): 'And Allah loves those who keep themselves clean.' Cleanliness earns Allah's love.

mcqs.q: Taharah is a part of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is faith. The Prophet ﷺ said cleanliness is a part (half, in the wording of the Hadith) of faith. The matching exercise also completes the sentence 'Taharah is a part of — faith'.

mcqs.q: Using the Miswak is a cause of cleanliness of the mouth and of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the pleasure of the Lord. The lesson quotes that the Miswak brings cleanliness of the mouth and Allah's pleasure together. That is why the Prophet ﷺ loved using it.

lessons.title: Sadaqat — Truthfulness
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Sadaqat

  • Sadaqat means truthfulness; it is derived from "Sidq", which means speaking the truth and stating a matter according to reality.
  • In good morals, truthfulness is a high quality; one who speaks the truth is called Sadiq.
  • Speaking the truth is the Sunnah of the Prophets; before Prophethood, the Holy Prophet ﷺ was famous for truthfulness.

Command of the Quran

Allah Almighty says: "O you who believe! Fear Allah and be with the truthful." (Surah At-Tawbah, Ayah 119). In the Holy Quran and the blessed Ahadith, great emphasis has been laid on truthfulness, and we are commanded to live with the truthful.

The Man with Four Bad Habits

A person came to the Holy Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have four bad habits: (1) stealing, (2) drinking wine, (3) adultery and (4) lying. How can I get rid of these evils?" The Prophet ﷺ said only this: "Promise not to lie." (By giving up lying, a person is saved from all evils.)

Benefits of Truthfulness

  • A truthful person holds an important position in society.
  • By adopting the habit of truthfulness, a person is saved from all evils.
  • By adopting truthfulness, the heart remains content.
  • A liar has no honour in the eyes of people; lying destroys the spirit of faith and goodness, and leads to Hell, while truthfulness leads to Paradise.
  • In a truthful Muslim, evils like betrayal and lying cannot develop; in matters of business and trade, adopting truthfulness is very necessary.

mcqs.q: Islam has commanded us to live with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the truthful. The Quran says: 'Fear Allah and be with the truthful' (At-Tawbah: 119), quoted in the lesson. Our company shapes our character.

mcqs.q: Before Prophethood, the Holy Prophet ﷺ was famous for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is truthfulness. Even before Prophethood, people knew him as Sadiq (the Truthful). The book's MCQ exercise gives this as his famous quality.

mcqs.q: One who speaks the truth is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sadiq. The lesson explains that Sadaqat comes from 'Sidq', speaking the truth. A liar is called Kadhib, the opposite of Sadiq.

mcqs.q: Sadaqat is derived from 'Sidq', which means:
options: Speaking the truth according to reality
mcqs.why: The correct answer is speaking the truth according to reality. The lesson defines Sidq as stating a matter just as it is. Truthfulness is a high quality in good morals.

mcqs.q: The person who came to the Prophet ﷺ had how many bad habits?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is four: stealing, drinking wine, adultery and lying. The lesson narrates that he himself counted these four evils. The Prophet ﷺ treated the root of them all — lying.

mcqs.q: What single advice did the Prophet ﷺ give to the man with four bad habits?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Promise not to lie'. The lesson shows that when a person stops lying, he is saved from all other evils too. Truthfulness is the key that locks every sin.

mcqs.q: Speaking the truth is the Sunnah of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Prophets. The fill-in exercise says speaking the truth is the Sunnah of the Prophets. All Prophets were truthful and taught truthfulness.

mcqs.q: By adopting the way of lying, the spirit of faith and goodness:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it is destroyed. The true/false exercise corrects the statement: lying destroys the spirit of faith and goodness. It also leads to Hell, while truthfulness leads to Paradise.

mcqs.q: In matters of business and trade, adopting what is very necessary?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is truthfulness. The fill-in exercise stresses truth in business and trade. A truthful trader earns both profit and honour.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct about a truthful person?
options: He has no honour among people
He holds an important position in society and his heart remains content
He is saved from hard work
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he holds an important position in society and his heart remains content. The lesson lists these among the benefits of truthfulness. It is the liar who has no honour in people's eyes.

lessons.title: Amanat — Trustworthiness
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Amanat

  • The word "Amanat" is derived from "Aman", which means peace, contentment and security.
  • Amanat means that a person should be clean and honest in his dealings, and should pay everyone's right fully, with complete honesty and trustworthiness.
  • Amanat is also: placing something with someone and taking back that very same thing; a person who has this quality is called Ameen.
  • The word opposite to Amanat is Khiyanat (betrayal).
  • Amanat is not limited only to property and financial things: hiding someone's secret is also Amanat, fulfilling someone's right is Amanat, and fulfilling the responsibilities entrusted to one is also Amanat.

Command of the Quran

Allah Almighty says: "Indeed, Allah commands you to deliver trusts to their owners." (Surah An-Nisa, Ayat 58)

The Prophet ﷺ — Sadiq and Ameen

  • Before Islam, the idolaters of Makkah called the Holy Prophet ﷺ by the title "Ameen"; before Prophethood he was called "Sadiq" and "Ameen".
  • The Prophet ﷺ, in conveying the trust of religion, was not prepared for even the slightest addition or reduction.
  • The Prophets (AS) conveyed the religion of Allah to their nations with utmost honesty.

Signs of a Hypocrite

  • The Prophet ﷺ stated the signs of a hypocrite to be three: when he speaks, he tells a lie; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; and if a trust is placed with him, he betrays it.
  • He in whom there is no Amanat, in him there is no faith.
  • Betrayal in Amanat is one of the signs of a hypocrite.

Amanat for a Student and its Benefit

  • A student becomes trustworthy by studying diligently and protecting himself from copying (cheating).
  • By acting upon Amanat, love, peace and contentment arise in society, no one's right is violated, and trust is established.

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ stated the signs of a hypocrite to be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The lesson lists them: lying when speaking, breaking promises, and betraying a trust. Betrayal in Amanat is thus a sign of hypocrisy.

mcqs.q: Amanat is called:
options: Taking something and not returning it
Placing something with someone and taking back that very same thing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is placing something with someone and taking back that very same thing. This is the definition chosen in the book's MCQ exercise. Keeping back a trust would be Khiyanat, betrayal.

mcqs.q: A person in whom the quality of Amanat is present is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ameen. The lesson explains that the trustworthy person is called Ameen, just as the Prophet ﷺ was titled Ameen by the people of Makkah. Siddiq is a title of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

mcqs.q: The word 'Amanat' is derived from 'Aman', which means:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is peace, contentment and security. The lesson gives this origin of the word Amanat. Where trusts are honoured, society enjoys exactly this peace and security.

mcqs.q: Which word comes in opposition to Amanat?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Khiyanat (betrayal). The true/false exercise corrects the claim about Diyanat: the opposite of Amanat is Khiyanat. Betraying a trust is a sign of a hypocrite.

mcqs.q: What does Allah Almighty command in Surah An-Nisa (58) about trusts?
options: To keep them safe for oneself
To deliver trusts to their owners
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to deliver trusts to their owners. The lesson quotes this verse: 'Indeed, Allah commands you to deliver trusts to their owners.' A trust must reach its rightful owner.

mcqs.q: He in whom there is no Amanat, in him there is no:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is faith. The fill-in exercise completes the Hadith in this way. Amanat and Iman go together; one without the other is incomplete.

mcqs.q: Which of these is also counted as Amanat?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is hiding someone's secret. The true/false exercise corrects the opposite claim: keeping a secret is also Amanat. Fulfilling rights and entrusted responsibilities are Amanat too.

mcqs.q: How can a student become trustworthy?
options: By studying diligently and avoiding copying (cheating)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is by studying diligently and avoiding copying. The lesson says this is one form of a student's trust. Cheating is a betrayal of the trust of education.

mcqs.q: By what titles did the people of Makkah call the Prophet ﷺ before Prophethood?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sadiq and Ameen. The lesson says the idolaters of Makkah themselves called him Ameen, the Trustworthy, because of his honesty. His truthfulness and trust were known to all.

lessons.title: Ihsan — Doing Good
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Ihsan

  • Ihsan is derived from "Husn", which means beauty, excellence and goodness.
  • Ihsan means treating others with such good conduct that their hearts become happy and they get comfort and peace.
  • Ihsan means paying someone more than his due right; Adl (justice), by contrast, means keeping regard for equality and paying the due right.
  • In reality, Ihsan is one of the attributes of Allah Almighty, and Allah likes those who do Ihsan and keeps them as friends.

Ihsan in the Holy Quran

  • "Indeed, Allah commands justice and goodness (Ihsan) and giving to relatives." (Surah An-Nahl, Ayat 90)
  • "And seek, through what Allah has given you, the goodness of the home of the Hereafter." (Al-Qasas, Ayat 77)
  • Indeed, Allah has commanded doing Ihsan.

Ihsan of the Prophet ﷺ

  • On the occasion of the Conquest of Makkah, the Holy Prophet ﷺ forgave all the idolaters of Makkah, who had done him every kind of harm and had become enemies of his life.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "Do good to the person who has done evil to you."
  • The whole life of the Prophet ﷺ passed in doing good to people.

Ihsan in Daily Life

  • By doing Ihsan, love and brotherhood arise in society among one another; it is an important cause of love, not hatred.
  • As a student, helping one's companions in preparing for the examination is also Ihsan.

mcqs.q: On the occasion of the Conquest of Makkah, what did the Prophet ﷺ do to his deadly enemies?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he forgave them. The lesson narrates this as the great example of Ihsan: those who had harmed him in every way were pardoned. This is doing good in return for evil.

mcqs.q: Ihsan means:
options: Doing evil in return for goodness
Paying more than the due right
mcqs.why: The correct answer is paying more than the due right. The lesson contrasts Adl — paying exactly the due right — with Ihsan, which goes beyond it. That extra goodness is what wins hearts.

mcqs.q: Allah Almighty does what to those who do Ihsan?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that He likes them. The MCQ exercise gives this, and the lesson adds that Allah keeps those who do Ihsan as friends. Ihsan is one of Allah's own attributes.

mcqs.q: Ihsan is derived from 'Husn', which means:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is beauty, excellence and goodness. The lesson gives this derivation of the word Ihsan. Doing Ihsan makes our conduct beautiful in the eyes of Allah and people.

mcqs.q: In reality, Ihsan is one of the:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is attributes of Allah Almighty. The fill-in exercise completes the sentence in exactly this way. Because Allah Himself is Muhsin, He loves Ihsan in His servants.

mcqs.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the one who does evil to you?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Do good to him'. The lesson quotes this saying of the Prophet ﷺ alongside his forgiveness at the Conquest of Makkah. Returning good for evil is the highest form of Ihsan.

mcqs.q: Adl (justice) means:
options: Stopping someone from paying a right
Keeping regard for equality and paying the due right
Paying more than the due right
mcqs.why: The correct answer is keeping regard for equality and paying the due right. The true/false exercise marks this correct. Paying MORE than the due right is Ihsan, one step above Adl.

mcqs.q: Doing Ihsan to someone is an important cause of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is love and brotherhood. The true/false exercise corrects the claim about hatred: Ihsan creates love in society. Good treatment melts hearts and joins people.

mcqs.q: For a student, which of these is also Ihsan?
options: Helping companions in preparing for the examination
mcqs.why: The correct answer is helping companions in preparing for the examination. The lesson gives this very example of a student's Ihsan. Kindness in small daily matters is also Ihsan.

mcqs.q: According to Surah An-Nahl (90), Allah commands justice, Ihsan and:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is giving to relatives. The verse quoted in the lesson says: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice and goodness and giving to relatives.' Relatives have a special right to our Ihsan.

lessons.title: Isar — Spirit of Sacrifice for Country and Nation
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Isar

  • The literal meaning of Isar is "to give preference".
  • Isar means sacrificing one's own need, fulfilling the needs of others and benefiting them — for example, staying hungry oneself and feeding another hungry person, bearing hardship oneself and caring for another's comfort, and giving importance to another over oneself.
  • The work done with the intention of benefiting another is called Isar (not the work done for one's own benefit).
  • Islam has emphasised adopting the habit of Isar; living nations always remain filled with the spirit of Isar.

Isar of the Ansar of Madinah

  • When the Prophet ﷺ established the bond of brotherhood between the Ansar and the Muhajirun, the Ansar happily accommodated the Muhajirun in their homes and made them partners in their properties.
  • Allah Almighty says: "And they give others preference over themselves, even though they themselves are in need." (Al-Hashr: 9)
  • This was the greatest demonstration of Isar, made by the Ansar of Madinah for the Muhajirun of Makkah.
  • The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever makes him (a needy person) a guest tonight, Allah Almighty will have mercy on him.

Isar in the Battle of Yarmouk

Some wounded Mujahideen were writhing with thirst. When water was brought to one of them, he pointed to the wounded man beside him: "Give him first." That one said the same for the next. By the time the water-carrier reached each of them, they had all been martyred one after another. Such a lofty example of Isar — sacrificing one's own life — is very rarely found.

Isar for Country and Nation

  • In the war of 1965 CE, people sold the goods of their homes for the defence of the country and stood in queues to donate blood for the wounded soldiers.
  • Helping victims financially and personally in natural calamities — storms, floods or earthquakes — is also Isar; the 2005 CE earthquake came in the mountainous areas of Kashmir, and the nation helped its victims.

mcqs.q: The literal meaning of Isar is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'giving preference'. Isar means preferring others over oneself — fulfilling their needs before one's own. The book's MCQ and true/false exercises both give this meaning.

mcqs.q: The greatest demonstration of Isar was made by the Ansar of Madinah for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Muhajirun of Makkah. The lesson says the Ansar sheltered them in their homes and made them partners in their property. Allah praised this in Surah Al-Hashr (9).

mcqs.q: If you want to see the spirit of Isar, remember:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Battle of Yarmouk. There, wounded Mujahideen, dying of thirst, each sent the water to the next man before drinking. The true/false exercise corrects any other battle name to Yarmouk.

mcqs.q: The Prophet ﷺ established the bond of what between the Muhajirun and the Ansar?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is brotherhood. The fill-in exercise gives this bond as the basis of the Ansar's Isar. Through it, the Muhajirun were received as real brothers.

mcqs.q: The work done with the intention of benefiting whom is called Isar?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is another person. The true/false exercise corrects the self-benefit version: Isar is benefiting others at one's own cost. Benefiting only oneself is the opposite of Isar.

mcqs.q: In the war of 1965 CE, people stood in queues to:
options: Donate blood for the wounded soldiers
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to donate blood for the wounded soldiers. The lesson also tells that people sold household goods for the country's defence. This was Isar for the nation in a difficult time.

mcqs.q: Living nations always remain filled with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the spirit of Isar. The fill-in exercise completes the sentence this way. A nation whose people prefer others over themselves stays alive and strong.

mcqs.q: The 2005 CE earthquake in Pakistan came in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the mountainous areas of Kashmir. The matching exercise gives this location for the 2005 earthquake. Helping its victims was a national example of Isar.

mcqs.q: What did Allah Almighty say about the Ansar in Surah Al-Hashr (9)?
options: They give others preference over themselves, even though they themselves are in need
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they give others preference over themselves despite their own need. This verse, quoted in the lesson, is the Quran's own praise of Isar. It defines Isar perfectly.

mcqs.q: What did the wounded Mujahid do when water was brought to him at Yarmouk?
options: Pointed to the wounded man beside him to be given water first
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he pointed to the wounded man beside him first. Each Mujahid did the same for the next, and all were martyred before the water returned. This is the lesson's unforgettable example of Isar.

lessons.title: Rights of Parents
lessons.notes_html:
What is Huqooq-ul-Ibad?

  • "Huqooq" is the plural of "Haq", which means an established thing.
  • Huqooq-ul-Ibad means the rights of the creation of Allah Almighty, that is, human beings. By fulfilling them, our society becomes worthy of comfort, peace, love and tranquillity.
  • Huqooq-ul-Ibad does not mean the rights of Allah — it means the rights of human beings.

Parents in the Holy Quran

  • Allah Almighty says: "If one of them reaches old age before you, or both, then do not even say 'Uff' to them, nor rebuke them, and speak to them a good word." (Bani Israeel, Ayat 23)
  • Children are commanded to do good with parents and to treat them well and with kindness, in worldly matters too.
  • Even if the parents are non-Muslim or idolaters, it has been commanded to treat them well.
  • Respecting parents is obligatory upon children.

Parents in the Hadith

  • The Prophet ﷺ said: "The pleasure of the Lord is in the pleasure of the father."
  • The Prophet ﷺ said: "That person is disgraced, disgraced, disgraced — the one in whose life the parents, or one of them, become old, and he does not serve them and remains deprived of entering Paradise."
  • A Companion came to the Prophet ﷺ and took advice about going on Jihad (and was directed to the service of his parents).

The Mother's Greater Right

  • Islam has commanded more to fulfil the rights of the mother.
  • The reason: the mother bears more hardships than the father in the upbringing of children.
  • Parents should be respected and obeyed, and addressed with respect, especially in their old age.

mcqs.q: According to the guidance of the Holy Quran, parents should be treated:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is well. The Quran commands doing good with parents, as the lesson's MCQ exercise states. Even their old age must be met with kindness, not harshness.

mcqs.q: If the mother and father reach old age, they should be addressed:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is with respect. Surah Bani Israeel (23), quoted in the lesson, forbids even saying 'Uff' to old parents or rebuking them. Only a good, gentle word may be spoken to them.

mcqs.q: In the light of the Hadith, the pleasure of the Lord is:
options: In the pleasure of the father
In the pleasure of the grandfather
In the pleasure of the uncle
In the pleasure of the brother
mcqs.why: The correct answer is in the pleasure of the father. The lesson quotes this Hadith of the Prophet ﷺ. Pleasing one's parents is a way of pleasing Allah Himself.

mcqs.q: Even if the parents are idolaters, they should be treated:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is well. The MCQ and true/false exercises both confirm that idolater or non-Muslim parents must still be treated well. Disbelief of parents does not cancel their rights.

mcqs.q: 'Huqooq' is the plural of 'Haq', which means:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an established thing. The matching exercise gives this meaning of Haq. Huqooq-ul-Ibad are thus the fixed, established rights of human beings.

mcqs.q: Huqooq-ul-Ibad means:
options: The rights of the creation of Allah, i.e. human beings
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the rights of human beings, Allah's creation. The true/false exercise corrects the claim that it means Allah's rights. Fulfilling these rights brings peace and love to society.

mcqs.q: 'That person is disgraced, disgraced, disgraced' — the Prophet ﷺ said this about the one who:
options: Finds his parents old in his life and does not serve them, remaining deprived of Paradise
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the one who does not serve his aged parents. The lesson explains this Hadith in detail. Serving old parents is a door to Paradise, and neglecting them is disgrace.

mcqs.q: Why has Islam given more emphasis to the rights of the mother?
options: She bears more hardships than the father in the upbringing of children
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that she bears more hardships in bringing up children. The lesson gives this reason for the mother's greater right. Her sacrifices begin before the child's birth and continue for years.

mcqs.q: Respecting parents is what upon children?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is obligatory. The fill-in exercise says respecting parents is obligatory (farz-like duty) upon children. It is a command of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, not a matter of choice.

mcqs.q: A Companion came to the Prophet ﷺ to take advice about going on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Jihad. The fill-in exercise records that a Companion sought advice about Jihad and was directed towards serving his parents. Parents' service carries a reward like Jihad.

mcqs.q: What does the Quran command when parents reach old age?
options: Not even to say 'Uff' to them, nor rebuke them, and to speak a good word
mcqs.why: The correct answer is not even to say 'Uff', nor rebuke them, and to speak a good word. This is Surah Bani Israeel, verse 23, quoted fully in the lesson. Even the smallest word of annoyance is forbidden.

mcqs.q: In worldly matters, parents should be treated:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is with good behaviour. The true/false exercise marks this statement correct. Kindness to parents covers both religious and worldly dealings.

mcqs.q: Complete the command: 'And do ______ with parents.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'good'. The fill-in exercise completes the Quranic command as 'do good with parents'. This one word covers obedience, service, respect and kindness.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Islam commanded children to treat parents with kindness
Islam freed children from parents' rights
Parents should serve the children only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Islam commanded children to treat parents with kindness. The true/false exercise marks this correct. Both mother and father have rights, with extra emphasis on the mother.

mcqs.q: By fulfilling Huqooq-ul-Ibad, our society becomes worthy of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is comfort, peace, love and tranquillity. The lesson defines Huqooq-ul-Ibad by this fruit. Rights fulfilled means a society at peace.

lessons.title: Rights of Children
lessons.notes_html:
Children — A Blessing, Not a Burden

  • Children are, for parents, a great blessing from Allah Almighty — not a burden or a calamity.
  • Children are innocent and like flowers; our beloved Prophet Muhammad ﷺ used to love children immensely.
  • Islam came and abolished the cruel customs of the Age of Ignorance: killing children and burying baby girls alive in graves.

Rights of Children upon Parents

  • Islam has fixed the rights of children upon parents.
  • Parents should arrange their children's upbringing, training, education and marriage in a good manner.
  • Parents should arrange religious education for their children and provide a good and pure environment in the home.
  • According to need and means, children should be given higher education.
  • If there is means, parents should perform the Aqiqah of their children.
  • For the physical training of children, they should be given opportunities for games and play.

Equal Treatment

  • Parents should keep equal and fair treatment with every child.
  • Boys and girls should be treated with the same treatment; no one should be preferred over another, otherwise children become victims of a feeling of deprivation.

Gentle Training

  • The minor mischiefs of small children should be forgiven (overlooked).
  • Repeatedly stopping, scolding and beating children without reason damages their self-respect.
  • Criticising children in front of friends affects their mental growth; children should not be criticised and beaten in front of friends.

mcqs.q: Children are, for parents, from Allah Almighty:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a blessing. The MCQ and true/false exercises both reject 'burden' and call children a great blessing from Allah. They are a trust to be raised well, not a load to resent.

mcqs.q: For the minor mischiefs of small children, parents should:
options: Leave them to their own state
mcqs.why: The correct answer is forgive them. The lesson says the small mischiefs of little children should be overlooked. Harshness over every small fault harms the child.

mcqs.q: Stopping, scolding and beating children without reason:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it damages their self-respect. The lesson also warns that criticising children before friends harms their mental growth. Training must be gentle and wise.

mcqs.q: For the physical training of children, give them opportunities for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is games and play. The MCQ exercise gives play as the means of children's physical training. A healthy body is part of a child's rights.

mcqs.q: Which cruel customs of the Age of Ignorance did Islam abolish?
options: Killing children and burying baby girls alive
mcqs.why: The correct answer is killing children and burying baby girls alive. The lesson names these among the most cruel customs of Jahiliyyah. Islam protected the life and honour of children, especially girls.

mcqs.q: Children are innocent and like:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is flowers. The fill-in exercise uses this tender comparison. Like flowers, children need gentle care to grow and bloom.

mcqs.q: Our beloved Prophet Muhammad ﷺ used to do what with children?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is love them immensely. The fill-in exercise states this about the Prophet ﷺ. His kindness to children is the model for all parents.

mcqs.q: Boys and girls should be treated with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the same, equal treatment. The lesson warns that preferring one child over another makes the others feel deprived. Fairness among children is their right.

mcqs.q: If there is means, what should parents perform for their children?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Aqiqah. The true/false exercise marks it correct that parents with means should perform their children's Aqiqah. It is among the early rights of a newborn.

mcqs.q: According to need and means, children should be given:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is higher education. The matching exercise completes: 'According to need and means — children should be given higher education.' Parents must also arrange religious education and a good environment.

lessons.title: Rights of Teachers
lessons.notes_html:
High Status of the Teacher

  • In society, the teacher is regarded with a look of honour and respect; Islam has given the teacher an extremely high and superior status.
  • Islam has given the teacher the status of relation with the Prophets.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "I was sent as a teacher", and: "Scholars are the heirs of the Prophets."
  • Islam is the only religion which has given guidance in every walk of life.
  • In Western countries too, the teacher is regarded with a look of utmost respect, as high and exalted.

Sayings about the Teacher

  • Hazrat Ali (RA) said: "Whoever taught me even one letter made me his slave."
  • Hazrat Luqman, advising his son, said: "Always honour and respect your teacher even more than your parents."

Rights and Etiquettes of the Teacher

  • The teacher is like a spiritual father to the students, so he should be respected like a father.
  • One should not raise one's voice above the teacher's voice.
  • One should obey the teacher's orders.
  • When meeting the teacher, one should take the lead in greeting (salam).
  • One should always behave with the teacher with respect.
  • The more a student respects his teacher, the more he will be adorned with the ornament of knowledge.
  • The society in which the honour and rights of the teacher are cared for always progresses, and good citizens are produced there.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Ali (RA) said that whoever taught me even one letter made me:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'his slave'. This saying, quoted in the lesson, shows the extreme respect owed to a teacher. Even one letter of knowledge creates a lifelong debt of honour.

mcqs.q: The status that Islam has given to the teacher is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is extremely high and superior. Islam even relates the teacher to the Prophets, whose heirs the scholars are. No ordinary status matches this.

mcqs.q: In Western civilization and culture, the teacher is regarded:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is with a look of respect. The MCQ exercise notes that even in the West the teacher is held high and exalted. Respect for teachers is a universal value that Islam taught first.

mcqs.q: The society in which the honour and rights of the teacher are cared for always:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is progresses. The lesson says good citizens are produced in such a society. Nations rise when teachers are honoured.

mcqs.q: What did the Holy Prophet ﷺ say about himself regarding teaching?
options: I was sent as a king
I was sent as a teacher
I was sent as a trader
I was sent as a judge
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I was sent as a teacher'. This Hadith, quoted in the lesson, gives teaching the noblest rank. The Prophet ﷺ also called scholars the heirs of the Prophets.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Luqman advised his son to respect the teacher even more than:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his parents. The lesson quotes Luqman's advice to honour the teacher even beyond parents. This shows the teacher's rank as a spiritual father.

mcqs.q: One's own voice above the teacher's voice:
options: Should be raised only in debate
mcqs.why: The correct answer is should not be raised. This is one of the etiquettes listed in the lesson and its matching exercise. Speaking softly before a teacher is part of respect.

mcqs.q: The more a student respects his teacher, the more he will be adorned with the ornament of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is knowledge. The fill-in exercise completes the sentence in this way. Respect opens the heart to receive the teacher's knowledge.

mcqs.q: Islam has given the teacher the status of relation with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Prophets. The fill-in exercise says Islam related the teacher to the Prophets, and scholars are their heirs. Teaching is thus a prophetic profession.

mcqs.q: The teacher is like what to the students?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a spiritual father. The lesson says the teacher should therefore be respected like a father. He builds the student's soul and character, not only the mind.

lessons.title: Rights of Neighbours
lessons.notes_html:
Who is a Neighbour?

  • A neighbour is one whose house is near your house; the houses around and in the neighbourhood are all counted as neighbours.
  • It is narrated from Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) that the Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "The circle of the neighbours' rights extends to forty houses to the right and left, front and back."
  • The employees of one factory and the students of one teacher are also included in the neighbourhood.

Neighbours in the Holy Quran

Allah Almighty says: "And worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, and do good to parents, and to relatives, and to orphans, and to the needy, and to the neighbour who is a relative, and to the stranger neighbour, and to the close companion." (An-Nisa: 36). The commands of Islam about neighbours are stated very clearly.

Hadith about Neighbours

The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "That person can never be a believer who himself eats his fill, but his neighbour remains hungry." One who troubles a neighbour cannot be a (true) Muslim.

Rights of Neighbours

  • Share in the neighbours' sorrows and joys, and become equal partners in them.
  • Always look after the comfort and peace of the neighbours; never do anything that causes trouble to a neighbour.
  • Behave with neighbours with good conduct.
  • If a neighbour deserves help, help him according to one's means.
  • Send some portion of the things to eat and drink to the neighbours.
  • Give the poor neighbours also the status of equality, so that they remain happy and their self-respect is not hurt.

mcqs.q: One should behave with neighbours:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is with good conduct. Islam's commands about neighbours are very clear, as the lesson's matching exercise says. Good conduct with neighbours is a sign of faith.

mcqs.q: Give the poor neighbours also the status of equality so that they:
options: Fall victim to a feeling of deprivation
mcqs.why: The correct answer is so that they remain happy. The lesson adds that equality protects the poor neighbour's self-respect from being hurt. Rich and poor neighbours share the same rights.

mcqs.q: One who troubles a neighbour:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he cannot be a (true) Muslim. The MCQ exercise gives this severe warning. Troubling a neighbour contradicts the very spirit of Islam.

mcqs.q: That person can never be a believer who eats his fill while his neighbour remains:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is hungry. This Hadith, quoted in the lesson, makes feeding and caring for the neighbour a test of faith. A full stomach beside a hungry neighbour is not true belief.

mcqs.q: According to the Hadith, the circle of the neighbourhood extends to how many houses?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is forty houses. Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ fixed the circle of neighbours' rights at forty houses on every side — right, left, front and back.

mcqs.q: One should do what in every sorrow and joy of the neighbour?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is share in them. The lesson lists becoming equal partners in neighbours' sorrows and joys as their right. A neighbour is a partner in life, not a stranger.

mcqs.q: What should be sent to the neighbours from the things to eat and drink?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is some portion. The fill-in exercise says a portion of food and drink should be sent to neighbours. Sharing food is a simple, daily way of fulfilling their rights.

mcqs.q: Which of these are also included in the neighbourhood?
options: The employees of one factory and the students of one teacher
Only people of one street in another city
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the employees of one factory and the students of one teacher. The matching exercise extends 'neighbour' beyond houses to those who share a workplace or a class. Their rights are like neighbours' rights.

mcqs.q: In Surah An-Nisa (36), doing good is commanded to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy and:
options: The neighbour who is a relative and the stranger neighbour
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the neighbour who is a relative and the stranger neighbour. The verse quoted in the lesson names both kinds of neighbours. Near or far, related or stranger — every neighbour has a right.

mcqs.q: If a neighbour deserves help, then one should:
options: Help him according to one's means
Help only if he is rich
mcqs.why: The correct answer is help him according to one's means. The matching exercise completes the sentence in this way. Even small help, given sincerely, fulfils the neighbour's right.

chapters.title: Mashahir-e-Islam — Khadija, Ali, Data Ganj Bakhsh, Tariq bin Ziyad

lessons.title: Hazrat Khadija-tul-Kubra (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Family Background

  • Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was born in a noble family of the Quraish; her respected father's name was "Khuwailid".
  • She was a very pious woman; even before accepting Islam, she was famous in Arabia by the title of "Tahirah" (the Pure) — not "Siddiqah".

Trade and Marriage

  • Hazrat Khadijah (RA) had trade on a large scale and used to give her goods to people for trade; she was in search of a person unmatched in honesty and trustworthiness in dealings.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ went to the country of Syria (Sham) carrying the trade goods of Hazrat Khadijah (RA); a person named "Maisarah" was her servant.
  • Her nikah was solemnised by Hazrat Abu Talib; at the time of nikah, her age was 40 years and the blessed age of the Holy Prophet ﷺ was 25 years.

Service of Islam

  • Hazrat Khadijah (RA) is the only woman of Islam who accepted Islam before everyone else.
  • She devoted all her wealth and property to Islam.
  • During the preaching of Islam, she bore the cruelties and hardships of the polytheists of Makkah and fulfilled the role of a wise wife in a good manner.
  • It is narrated from Hazrat Ali (RA) that the Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "The most honoured and virtuous woman is Maryam bint Imran, and the most honoured and virtuous woman is Khadijah bint Khuwailid."
  • All the children of the Holy Prophet ﷺ were from Hazrat Khadijah (RA) except Hazrat Ibrahim (RA).
  • She passed away at the age of 65 years; the year of her passing and of Hazrat Abu Talib's passing is called "Aam-ul-Huzn" (the Year of Sorrow).

mcqs.q: A person named 'Maisarah' was to Hazrat Khadijah (RA):
mcqs.why: The correct answer is servant. The book's MCQ exercise identifies Maisarah as Hazrat Khadijah's (RA) servant, who accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the trade journey. His report of the journey impressed her greatly.

mcqs.q: The nikah of Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was solemnised by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Abu Talib. He was the uncle of the Holy Prophet ﷺ and head of the family. The MCQ exercise names him as the one who solemnised the nikah.

mcqs.q: The age of Hazrat Khadijah (RA) at the time of her passing was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 65 years. Both the MCQ and the true/false exercises confirm this age. She spent her whole life in the service of Islam.

mcqs.q: All the children of the Holy Prophet ﷺ were from Hazrat Khadijah (RA) except:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Ibrahim (RA). He was the son of Hazrat Mariah (RA), not of Hazrat Khadijah (RA). All the other children of the Prophet ﷺ were from Khadijah (RA).

mcqs.q: Before accepting Islam, Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was famous by the title of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Tahirah, the Pure. The true/false exercise corrects 'Siddiqah' to 'Tahirah'. Her purity was famous in Arabia even before Islam.

mcqs.q: The name of the father of Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Khuwailid. She is therefore also called Khadijah bint Khuwailid, as in the Hadith quoted in the lesson. She belonged to a noble family of the Quraish.

mcqs.q: The Holy Prophet ﷺ went to which country carrying the trade goods of Hazrat Khadijah (RA)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Syria (Sham). The fill-in exercise gives this journey, on which his honesty in trade was displayed. It led to her proposal of marriage.

mcqs.q: At the time of nikah, the ages of Hazrat Khadijah (RA) and the Holy Prophet ﷺ were:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: she was 40 years and he was 25 years. The true/false exercise corrects the reversed statement. Their marriage is a model of trust and companionship.

mcqs.q: The year of the passing of Hazrat Khadijah (RA) and Hazrat Abu Talib is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Aam-ul-Huzn, the Year of Sorrow. The true/false exercise marks this correct. The Prophet ﷺ lost his wife and his uncle in the same year.

mcqs.q: What is special about Hazrat Khadijah (RA) in accepting Islam?
options: She accepted Islam last of all
She is the woman who accepted Islam before everyone else
She accepted Islam after the Hijrah
She never met the Prophet ﷺ
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that she accepted Islam before everyone else. The lesson calls her the only woman who believed first of all people. She also devoted all her wealth to Islam.

lessons.title: Hazrat Ali-ul-Murtaza (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Family and Childhood

  • Hazrat Ali (RA) was born in the Holy Ka'bah (Baitullah Sharif). His name was "Ali"; his kunniyat were "Abul Hasan" and "Abu Turab".
  • His father's name was Hazrat Abu Talib, and his noble mother's name was "Fatimah bint Asad"; his mother had given him the title of "Haider".
  • When Hazrat Ali (RA) was young, the Holy Prophet ﷺ took the responsibility of his upbringing into his own hands (not Hazrat Abbas (RA)).

Acceptance of Islam and Services

  • At the announcement of Prophethood, Hazrat Ali (RA) was only ten years old; among children, he was the first to accept Islam.
  • Obeying the order of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, he returned all the trusts to their owners, and after returning the trusts he met the Holy Prophet ﷺ at the place of "Quba".
  • When the disbelievers came to know in the morning about the Hijrah of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, they became very disappointed.
  • He took part in all the Ghazwat except Ghazwa Tabuk.
  • In Ghazwa Khaibar, he killed the famous Jewish wrestler Marhab.
  • He sold his armour to buy the necessary goods for his wedding; his nikah was solemnised by the Holy Prophet ﷺ himself, who performed his nikah with Hazrat Fatimah (RA).

Caliphate and Martyrdom

  • Hazrat Ali (RA) took over the reins of the Caliphate in the year 35 AH and held them until 40 AH.
  • He was the first Caliph among the Khulafa-e-Rashideen who shifted the capital from Madinah Munawwarah to Kufa, keeping in view the conditions and the administration.
  • A wretched Khariji, Abdur Rahman bin Muljim, struck him with a poisoned sword while he was going to the mosque for the Fajr prayer.
  • On the third day, on 21 Ramadan-ul-Mubarak, 40 AH (not 21 Shaban), he attained the rank of martyrdom; his caliphate lasted four years and nine months.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Ali (RA) took part in all the Ghazwat except:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ghazwa Tabuk. The MCQ and true/false exercises agree that he did not take part in Tabuk, as he was left in Madinah. He fought bravely in all the other battles, including Khaibar.

mcqs.q: In the morning, when the disbelievers came to know of the Hijrah of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, they:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they became very disappointed. Their plan had failed: the Prophet ﷺ had left safely while Hazrat Ali (RA) lay on his bed. Disappointment is the word used in the book's exercise.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Ali (RA) sold his armour and bought necessary goods for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the wedding. The exercise says he sold his armour to arrange the necessities of his marriage with Hazrat Fatimah (RA). This shows his simplicity and poverty despite his rank.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Ali (RA) took over the reins of the Caliphate in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 35 AH. He held the Caliphate until 40 AH, for four years and nine months. In 40 AH he was martyred.

mcqs.q: One of the kunniyat of Hazrat Ali (RA) was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Abul Hasan. The fill-in and matching exercises give his two kunniyat as Abul Hasan and Abu Turab. His mother had titled him 'Haider'.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Ali (RA) killed the famous Jewish wrestler ______ in Ghazwa Khaibar:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Marhab. The fill-in exercise names him as the champion killed by Hazrat Ali (RA) at Khaibar. This connects with the Khyber lesson in Unit 3.

mcqs.q: Keeping the conditions in view, Hazrat Ali (RA) shifted the capital from ______ to Kufa:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Madinah Munawwarah. The lesson explains he moved the capital to Kufa for administration and to manage the mischief-makers. He was the first Caliph to do so.

mcqs.q: The nikah of Hazrat Ali (RA) was solemnised by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Holy Prophet ﷺ himself. The fill-in and matching exercises state that the Messenger ﷺ performed his nikah with Hazrat Fatimah (RA). It was a simple and blessed ceremony.

mcqs.q: Among children, who was the first to accept Islam?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Ali (RA), at the age of only ten years. The true/false exercise marks this correct. He believed in the Prophet ﷺ at the very announcement of Prophethood.

mcqs.q: When Hazrat Ali (RA) was young, who brought him up?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Holy Prophet ﷺ. The true/false exercise corrects the claim about Hazrat Abbas (RA): the Prophet ﷺ himself took charge of Ali's upbringing. Ali (RA) thus grew up in the Prophet's ﷺ own home.

mcqs.q: The martyrdom of Hazrat Ali (RA) took place on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 21 Ramadan, 40 AH. The true/false exercise corrects the month from Shaban to Ramadan. He was struck with a poisoned sword by Abdur Rahman bin Muljim while going for Fajr prayer.

mcqs.q: Who struck Hazrat Ali (RA) with a poisoned sword?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Abdur Rahman bin Muljim, a wretched Khariji. The lesson narrates that he attacked Hazrat Ali (RA) on the way to the mosque for Fajr. Ali (RA) was martyred on the third day after the attack.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Ali (RA) was born in:
options: The house of the Prophet ﷺ
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Holy Ka'bah. The lesson states this unique honour of Hazrat Ali (RA). No one else holds this distinction of birth inside Baitullah.

mcqs.q: After returning the trusts to their owners, Hazrat Ali (RA) met the Holy Prophet ﷺ at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Quba. The matching exercise gives this meeting place after the Hijrah night, when Ali (RA) had returned every trust. Trustworthiness marked his whole life.

mcqs.q: The name of the noble mother of Hazrat Ali (RA) was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Fatimah bint Asad. The lesson names her as his mother; she gave him the title 'Haider'. His father was Hazrat Abu Talib.

lessons.title: Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh Ali Hujwiri (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Birth and Family

  • Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh (RA) was born in the region of "Hajwer" in Afghanistan in the year 400 AH, corresponding to 1009 CE; for this reason he is called "Hajweri".
  • His real name was "Ali", and his father's name was Usman.
  • The title "Ganj Bakhsh" means the bestower of the spiritual treasure.

Search for Knowledge and Arrival in Lahore

  • He travelled to different countries for forty years to seek knowledge.
  • After completing his academic and spiritual training, he went to Lahore.
  • As soon as he came to Lahore, he became busy in the preaching of the religion.
  • He conveyed the message of Islam to the common people through his good deeds and the preaching of religion; thousands of non-Muslims accepted Islam at his blessed hand.

His Book and Passing

  • He wrote many books on different subjects; his famous book "Kashf-ul-Mahjoob" gained great fame and also contains the teaching of ethics.
  • His book written in the Persian language is on the subject of Tasawwuf (Sufism).
  • His passing away took place in the year 465 AH, corresponding to 1072 CE.

mcqs.q: The real name of Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh (RA) was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ali. 'Usman' was his father's name — a trap in the book's own MCQ. His full name is therefore Ali Hujwiri, and 'Data Ganj Bakhsh' is his famous title.

mcqs.q: After completing his academic and spiritual training, Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh (RA):
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Lahore. He settled in Lahore and made it the centre of his preaching. His shrine there is still visited by thousands.

mcqs.q: As soon as Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh (RA) came to Lahore, he became busy in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the preaching of the religion. The MCQ exercise gives this as his first work in Lahore. Through his preaching and good deeds, thousands accepted Islam.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh (RA) travelled to different countries for how many years to seek knowledge?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is forty years. The fill-in exercise gives this long period of travel for knowledge. Only after this training did he settle in Lahore.

mcqs.q: The passing away of Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh (RA) took place in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 465 AH, corresponding to 1072 CE. The year 400 AH / 1009 CE is his year of birth, not of passing. He lived about sixty-five years.

mcqs.q: Thousands of non-Muslims accepted what at his blessed hand?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Islam. The fill-in exercise records that thousands embraced Islam through him. His good character was itself the strongest preaching.

mcqs.q: His famous book 'Kashf-ul-Mahjoob' is written in Persian on the subject of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Tasawwuf (Sufism). The fill-in exercise says the Persian book is on Tasawwuf. Kashf-ul-Mahjoob is the most famous of his many books and also teaches ethics.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh (RA) was born in which region?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hajwer, in Afghanistan, in 400 AH / 1009 CE. That is why he is called 'Hajweri' (or Hujwiri). Lahore was his later home, not his birthplace.

mcqs.q: What does the title 'Ganj Bakhsh' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is bestower of the spiritual treasure. The lesson explains this famous title: people received the treasure of faith and spirituality from him. 'Ganj' means treasure and 'Bakhsh' means bestower.

mcqs.q: The name of the father of Hazrat Data Ganj Bakhsh (RA) was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Usman. The lesson states his real name was Ali and his father's name was Usman. The two names are easily confused, so the book asks them separately.

lessons.title: Hazrat Tariq bin Ziyad (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Who was Tariq bin Ziyad?

  • Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) is counted among the best commanders.
  • He was the general of Musa bin Nusair, who had conquered Africa and established an Islamic empire there.
  • Musa bin Nusair sent his general Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) towards Spain with an army of about seven thousand, to free its people from the cruelty of "Roderick".
  • In the era of Banu Umayyah, the message of Islam was reaching the far-flung regions of the world, and under the leadership of Tariq bin Ziyad the Islamic army advanced towards Spain.

The Conquest of Spain

  • Spain is a country of the continent of Europe; before the arrival of the Muslims, the people of Europe were drowned in ignorance.
  • Spain was ruled by the Christian king "Roderick", a great cruel and tyrant king.
  • The mountain near which Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) pitched tents is called Jabal-ul-Tariq.
  • Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) gave an emotional (stirring) speech to the Mujahideen; it affected them as if electricity had run through them.
  • Raising the slogan of Takbeer (Allahu Akbar), they fought against the enemy's army of one hundred thousand; fierce battle continued continuously, and King Roderick was killed at the hands of Tariq bin Ziyad (RA).
  • Spain was conquered in the year 711 CE.

Muslim Spain

  • The Muslims ruled Spain for about seven hundred years.
  • Even today in Spain, the magnificent grand mosque of Granada and the splendid building of Alhambra and other structures of that era exist (they are in Spain, not Saudi Arabia).
  • The Muslims built beautiful buildings in Spain, one of which is named Alhambra.

mcqs.q: Before the arrival of the Muslims, the people of Europe were:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is drowned in ignorance. The book's MCQ exercise describes Europe before Islam's arrival in this way. Muslim Spain later became a centre of learning for the whole continent.

mcqs.q: The Muslims built beautiful buildings in Spain, one of which is named:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Alhambra. This splendid palace of Granada is named in the lesson as a jewel of Muslim Spain. The Taj Mahal is in India and Burj Khalifa is modern.

mcqs.q: Spain is situated in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the continent of Europe. The lesson says Spain is a European country ruled at that time by Christians. Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) crossed from Africa to conquer it.

mcqs.q: Spain was conquered in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 711 CE. Note the trap: 711 AH would be centuries later. The conquest of Spain by Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) took place in 711 CE.

mcqs.q: The mountain near which Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) pitched tents is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Jabal-ul-Tariq, the Mountain of Tariq. The fill-in and true/false exercises both give this name. It is the famous rock known today as Gibraltar.

mcqs.q: Spain was ruled by the king:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Roderick. The lesson calls him a great cruel and tyrant king, from whose cruelty the people were to be freed. Heraclius ruled Rome and Kisra ruled Persia.

mcqs.q: The Muslims ruled Spain for about:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is about seven hundred years. The fill-in exercise gives this long period of Muslim rule in Spain. Its monuments, like Alhambra, still stand today.

mcqs.q: Who sent Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) to Spain, and with how much army?
options: Musa bin Nusair, with about 7,000 men
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Musa bin Nusair, with about seven thousand men. The lesson says Musa, the conqueror of Africa, sent his general Tariq. With this small army he defeated Roderick's one hundred thousand.

mcqs.q: What effect did the address of Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) have on the Mujahideen?
options: It affected them as if electricity had run through them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it affected them as if electricity had run through them. The lesson uses these words for his emotional speech. Full of zeal, they raised the Takbeer and fought bravely.

mcqs.q: King Roderick was killed at the hands of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Tariq bin Ziyad (RA). The true/false and matching exercises state that Spain's king and commander Roderick was killed at his hands. With his fall, Spain was conquered.

mcqs.q: What was the size of the enemy army that the Muslims faced in Spain?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one hundred thousand. The lesson contrasts this huge army with Tariq's about seven thousand Mujahideen. Firm intention and passion, not numbers, brought the victory.

mcqs.q: The magnificent grand mosque of Granada and the Alhambra are in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Spain. The true/false exercise corrects the claim that they are in Saudi Arabia. These buildings still exist in Spain as remains of the Muslim era.

mcqs.q: Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) was the general of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Musa bin Nusair. The lesson introduces Tariq as Musa's general; Musa had conquered Africa. Tariq then carried the campaign into Spain under his leadership.

mcqs.q: In which era did the message of Islam reach the far-flung regions of the world, including Spain?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the era of Banu Umayyah. The matching exercise completes the sentence with this era. The conquest of Spain in 711 CE belongs to Umayyad times.

mcqs.q: Why was Tariq bin Ziyad (RA) sent towards Spain?
options: To free its people from the cruelty of Roderick
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to free its people from the cruelty of Roderick. The lesson gives this purpose of the expedition. Islam's armies came as liberators from tyranny, not as looters.
